cadence_note: One story every 2 days. The performance analyst may move this between 2 and 3 days based on results.
post_hour_uk: around 13:00-14:00 (lunch scroll), scheduled post_delay_minutes after review
spicy_means: on-pitch drama: red cards, meltdowns, bust-ups with team-mates or opponents, famous confrontations
public fallouts with managers or clubs that the people involved confirmed or that 2+ trusted outlets reported
transfer sagas: completed or officially collapsed moves, hold-outs, release clauses, the quotes around them
rejection to stardom: released by an academy, written off, came back
rivalries and trash talk on the record
wild but official facts: contract clauses, records, fines and bans handed down by a club or federation
controversial decisions and their fallout (VAR, bans, appeals) as officially reported
never: private life: relationships, partners, family, children, homes, money outside football
health or mental health beyond what the player has said publicly
criminal allegations, court cases, arrests, betting allegations
rumours, 'sources say', unconfirmed reports, transfer gossip
anything sexual, tragedy or death, race, religion, nationality, appearance
mocking injuries; calling anyone a fraud, cheat or liar; 'exposed' framing
living players' stories that are only spicy because they are cruel
evidence: Every fact needs 2 trusted outlets (config/teams.json research.trusted_domains) or 1 official source; quotes verbatim from a trusted outlet with who/when/where. If a key beat can't be confirmed, drop it or pick another story.

structure.note: the most dramatic moment first (in medias res), payoff within 3 s, max 10 words
CHAPTER 1: who, where, when; year on the card
CHAPTER 2: what went wrong / the clash
the turn: an on-record quote or the unexpected outcome
where it ended up, with a real number
open loop or debate question + 'follow for the next Scout File'

hook_styles: In medias res: 'He was released at 15. Ten years later, they paid 80 million to get him back.'
Contradiction: 'His manager called him unprofessional. He won the league the next season.'
Number shock: 'Fourteen red cards. One player.'
Open loop: 'One phone call ended his time at the club.'
topic_sources: data/trends/<latest>.json (players fans are talking about now)
topic_rules: Prefer a player who is trending this week (the story answers 'why is everyone talking about him?'). Rotate clubs; no club twice in a row; mix favourites and rivals. Never repeat a story in data/stories/state.json.
